faq: It depends on scope. A landing page or brand site can land in 1-2 weeks, while a full WordPress build, e-commerce store or custom plugin usually runs 3-6 weeks including revisions.
Do you work with WordPress page builders or custom code?
Both. Most projects start in Elementor or a similar builder for speed, then move into custom PHP, JavaScript and CSS wherever the build needs something a page builder can't do on its own.
Can you take over an existing website?
Yes. A lot of the work in this portfolio is maintenance, fixes and new features added to sites I did not originally build.
Do you work with clients remotely?
Yes, every project in this portfolio was delivered remotely, for clients across Nigeria, the UK, Canada and the USA.
What do you need from me to get started?
Access to the hosting/domain (or a plan for getting it), any brand assets you already have, and a short description of what the site needs to do. I can help fill in the gaps from there.

highlights.title: CFM Waitlist
highlights.subtitle: Custom WordPress Event Management Plugin
paragraphs: Built a bespoke WordPress plugin from scratch for CULTUR FM, a music and culture brand. The plugin manages the full event access lifecycle — waitlist, ticket sales, free signup, and sold-out states — all controlled via a simple admin toggle per event.

Key features include: a custom database table for subscriber management with duplicate detection and email confirmation, GDPR-compliant consent capture, CSV export and bulk email tools for event admins, and a dynamic front-end CTA that automatically renders the correct action based on event state.

On mobile, a fixed sticky bar stays anchored at the bottom of the screen; tapping it opens a modal form with a full dark overlay. The plugin integrates with Advanced Custom Fields and a custom post type, with all logic written in vanilla PHP, JavaScript, and CSS — no page builders, no third-party plugin dependencies.
skills: Custom WordPress plugin development (PHP, no framework)
Vanilla JS (AJAX, DOM manipulation, mobile UX)
CSS architecture (specificity, z-index stacking, mobile-first responsive)
WordPress hooks, AJAX handlers, nonce security
UX problem-solving (multi-state UI, sticky mobile CTA, modal management)
